entry.title: I Tested AWS Regional NAT Gateway — Here's Why It Changes Everything
entry.summary: Last week, I got my hands on the new Regional NAT Gateway for Amazon VPC. After spending a few hours testing it in a real environment, I wanted to share what I learned and why this matters for anyone building on AWS. Let me paint you a picture. You're running a three-tier application spread across three Availability Zones (us-east-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1c). Your backend servers sit in private subnets because, well, that's the right thing to do. But these servers need to reach the internet — maybe to pull security patches, call external APIs, or push logs to a third-party service. Three NAT Gateways. Three public subnets. Three separate route tables to maintain. And if you forgot to set up one AZ properly? Your workloads in that zone lose internet access. I've seen this go wrong more time…
